The CODYRUN software uses a nodal analysis approach to model the heat transfer in buildings, considering conduction, convection, and radiation.
The CODYRUN software couples the thermal and airflow modules through an iterative process, using a pressure model to calculate the inter-zonal airflow rates.
The CODYRUN software has been validated through inter-model comparisons with other building simulation tools and against experimental data from test cells and real buildings.
The air solar collector is modeled in CODYRUN as a zone with a glazed window, exterior walls, and an inner absorber wall, with a specific solar radiation absorption process.
The key parameters that influence the performance of a Trombe wall system are the external glazing emissivity, the window type, and the wall absorptivity.
The CODYRUN model is able to capture the inverse thermocirculation that can occur in a Trombe wall system, where the flow reverses at night and the system cools the room.
The impact of the hole closing system in the Trombe wall is relatively minor in the studied case, as the mass flow has low sensitivity to the opening state.

To improve the performance of a Trombe wall, increasing the wall surface area and/or adding reflectors to raise the incoming sunlight intensity could be effective, as well as using a double-glazed system.
The CODYRUN simulations provide a range of outputs for the Trombe wall system, including the conductive heat flux, the sensible power outputs, the global heat flux, and comfort indices.

The CODYRUN software uses a specific solar radiation absorption model for the air solar collector, as the solar irradiation typically does not directly impact an internal wall in building simulations.
The CODYRUN software has been validated through the BESTEST procedure, which involves simulating various buildings with increasing complexity and comparing the results with other simulation codes.
The CODYRUN software has recently been supplemented by a CO2 propagation model in buildings, in addition to the thermal and airflow modeling capabilities.
The CODYRUN software is able to handle the modeling of mechanical ventilation systems by considering their known airflow values, without the need for detailed flow-pressure characteristics.
The CODYRUN software uses a finite difference scheme for the numerical solution of the humidity transfer model, which includes the use of a hygroscopic buffer.

The CODYRUN software has been used to study the application of Trombe wall systems in a developing country context, such as classrooms in Antananarivo, Madagascar, to help address low temperatures during the winter season.
